title: Renewal & Expansion Check-in — Mantle Finance
next_steps: Jordan Lee - Send revised pricing with committed capacity tiers and regional add-ons by 2027-02-28
Samir Patel - Run a 2-region capacity benchmark (US-West + EU-West) and share perf/cost spreadsheet by 2027-03-03
Aisha Khan - Confirm final data residency and retention requirements by 2027-03-01
Claire Wu - Loop in legal for one-year extension wording and NDA addendum by 2027-03-05
action_items: Jordan Lee: Prepare renewal quote with 20% committed discount and optional burst capacity
Samir Patel: Validate Dedicated GPU sizing and expected latency at 1k TPS for inference peak windows
Ben Ortiz: Provide current regional traffic split and monthly token estimates
Aisha Khan: Share production prompt set for regression testing during POC
header: Date: 2027-02-24 | Start: 15:00 PST | Duration: 45m | Recording: yes | Location: Zoom
summary: Quarterly renewal and expansion check-in. Customer considering a 12-month renewal with a committed capacity increase (reserved GPUs), adding EU region for redundancy, and negotiating data residency + contract extension terms. Redwood AE + SE reviewed capacity options, benchmark plan, and pricing. Agreed next steps include a revised quote, capacity benchmark, and legal review.
topics: adding EU region and multi-region routing
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Jordan from Redwood. Samir and I are on. How are you all?
[00:05] Aisha Khan: Good, thanks. Hi Jordan, hi Samir.
[00:07] Ben Ortiz: Hey. Sorry running a bit late set up some VPN stuff.
[00:11] Jordan Lee: No worries. Quick agenda: renewal numbers, capacity increase, adding EU region, and any legal / data residency items. We have about 45 minutes.
[00:18] Claire Wu: Sounds good.
[00:20] Jordan Lee: Great. Aisha, maybe start — where are you on your internal approval for renewal and what are the top priorities?
[00:26] Aisha Khan: Yeah, so high level — Mantle wants to renew for 12 months. We're happy with Redwood's latency and quality, but we need more predictable capacity for end of quarter spikes. Also need EU region because we have EU customers and some residency asks. Main concerns are cost and ensuring the models we run don't regress after quantization — we've seen that before with other providers.
[00:46] Samir Patel: Totally — when you say predictable capacity for spikes, are you looking at Reserved Dedicated pools with burst options or a larger Hosted throughput commitment?
[00:55] Aisha Khan: Prefer Dedicated pools. We want isolated capacity and predictable tail latency.
[01:00] Ben Ortiz: And we need VPC peering for Private or Dedicated to meet our network security — not public internet.
[01:07] Jordan Lee: Understood. For Dedicated we can do reserved GPU pools; recommended sizing depends on your steady-state tokens and peak TPS. Ben, do you have rough monthly token numbers and peak concurrent requests?
[01:17] Ben Ortiz: Right now baseline is around 120M tokens/month, peaks hit ~1k inference requests per minute during batch reports. Latency target is sub-200ms p99 for single-turn prompts.
[01:29] Samir Patel: OK that's helpful. For 1k RPM with p99 <200ms, we typically recommend a Dedicated cluster with N x A10/A100 equivalent VMs — depends on model. If you're using a 7B style model quantized to int8, throughput is higher and cost lower. For GPT-scale models you need heavier GPUs.
[01:45] Aisha Khan: We're running two model families — a fine-tuned open model (7B-ish) for routing and a larger 13B for complex summarization. We want to avoid quality regressions on the 13B when we move to int8.
[01:58] Jordan Lee: Right; Redwood Optimize will flag quality drift and we can pin model variants. For the 13B we can recommend a mixed profile — keep 13B in fp16 on Dedicated for the critical paths and use quantized 7B for lower-latency tasks. That also helps keep cost down.
[02:13] Claire Wu: From contract perspective, procurement prefers a 12-month extension with monthly billing, but we're open to a slight upfront commit if there are better economics. Also need SSO + SCIM and SOC2 attestation copy.
[02:25] Jordan Lee: We can do SSO + SCIM and will share our SOC 2 report. For billing we can propose a committed monthly spend with a built-in burst credit bucket and a 20% discount at the tier you're targeting.
[02:36] Aisha Khan: Can you send sample contract language for the 12-month term? Also add the EU region add-on pricing.
[02:41] Jordan Lee: Absolutely. We'll include language for data residency addendum and KMS integration. One question on residency — do you need data to never leave EU physical servers or is logical segregation enough?
[02:52] Aisha Khan: Physical residency is preferred for some EU customers, so ideally EU data processed in EU-only, keys in our KMS in EU region.
[02:59] Samir Patel: That's doable with Redwood Private in a dedicated VPC or Dedicated with regional isolation. We support KMS/HSM integrations per region. We'll note that in the security doc.
[03:09] Ben Ortiz: For networking, we prefer VPC peering plus private endpoints not internet-facing.
[03:13] Samir Patel: We can configure private endpoints and peering, and help with firewall rules. We'll include the network runbook.
[03:20] Jordan Lee: On pricing for the EU region add-on — typically a 10-15% premium for dedicated capacity in additional region due to infra costs. We can show two options: 1) Active-active across US + EU with regional routing, or 2) Primary US, passive EU failover with warm standby. Which model do you prefer?
[03:36] Aisha Khan: Prefer active-active if cost allows; otherwise passive failover is acceptable for phase 1. Our customers expect low latency in EU so active-active helps.
[03:44] Jordan Lee: Noted. Samir, do you want to talk about the benchmark plan?
[03:48] Samir Patel: Sure — propose a 2-week benchmark: we'll provision a mirror Dedicated cluster for US-West and EU-West, run your prod prompt set (Aisha to provide) across target models, measure p95/p99 latency, cost per token at several batch sizes, and run regression checks. We can capture traces and KV/cache hit ratios. That should give confidence before commit.
[04:06] Aisha Khan: Two weeks is fine. We'll share the prompt set and a sample traffic replay file.
[04:11] Ben Ortiz: For the replay, note that we have spikes at month-end that are 3x baseline, so include those windows.
[04:18] Samir Patel: Good to know. We'll simulate those bursts. Also we'll test autoscale policies and burst credits so you get predictable behavior.
[04:25] Claire Wu: On the legal seat, I'm going to get our counsel to look at the extension language and start redlines. We prefer the one-year with an auto-renew clause unless either party gives 60-days notice.
[04:35] Jordan Lee: We can include that. On SLA, since you're moving to Dedicated we can offer a higher uptime SLA and dedicated support.
[04:41] Aisha Khan: Perfect. One more item — model governance and evals: we want regression alerts tied to our eval suite so any quality drop after quantization is flagged automatically.
[04:50] Samir Patel: Redwood Optimize supports eval sets and automatic regression alerts. We'll set up a dashboard per model and per release. We'll also include the eval results during the benchmark.
[04:59] Jordan Lee: Cool. Any blockers that would prevent you from signing if pricing and perf line up? Claire, procurement?
[05:05] Claire Wu: Legal review and data residency confirmation. Also need final quote to compare to internal budget, but nothing else major.
[05:12] Aisha Khan: From engineering side, we need the benchmark results before the commit.
[05:16] Jordan Lee: Sounds reasonable. Tentative timeline: we'll send revised pricing and contract language by 2/28, Samir will run bench and deliver results by 3/03, you confirm residency and legal by 3/05, and target sign by 3/10. Does that work?
[05:29] Ben Ortiz: Yes that timeline looks fine.
[05:31] Claire Wu: Works for procurement.
[05:33] Aisha Khan: Fine here.
[05:35] Jordan Lee: Great. Any other questions?
[05:37] Aisha Khan: Quick question — do you have references for another finance customer with EU region setup?
[05:42] Jordan Lee: We do; I can share a short case study (redacted) and reference contact.
[05:47] Ben Ortiz: Also can you itemize the networking steps for VPC peering? We'll need to provision on our side.
[05:53] Samir Patel: We'll send a runbook with steps and required firewall ports and CIDR ranges.
[05:57] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone. I'll recap next steps in an email after the call. Appreciate your time.
[06:03] Claire Wu: Thanks.
[06:04] Aisha Khan: Thank you.
[06:06] Ben Ortiz: Bye.
[06:07] Jordan Lee: Bye all.

Notes on transcript: occasional transcription artifacts: "KV cache" came out as "K-V cash" in a few spots; "Redwood Optimize" sometimes transcribed as "Red wood optimize". Some speaker labels merged during crosstalk.
